name: Ruskel

anatomy.part: crown of the wooden knob, on its top edge
the knot where the handle meets the spike (the brightest star)
the waist of the spike shaft
the point of the spike, where the rope-opening strands begin
left end of the grip bar
right end of the grip bar

myth: When Aun cut the string, the rope that held the sky came apart in his hands, and the sky went up with its ends frayed. Mother Hesk sent the Gulls down to say so. Nobody on the islands could splice a rope that long from below, so Ennu the Kite-Wright carved the first Ruskel from bone, thick at the knot and fine at the point, and gave it to the rope-makers. You push the point between the strands, you open a gap, you lay the new strand in and draw it through. Hesk says the same can be done to the sky. So at the rope-making feast the people hold up the Fid, and in autumn it rises over the Lamp Road, pointed at the place where the string was cut. Aun is not there. But the knot of his old tether still shows in the sky if you know where to look, and the Fid is always pointed at it, and never quite reaches.
verse:
Open the cut rope
with a bone point, slow and sure,
draw the new strand through.
